texts: The false statement is that DDI mode triggers a ventricular beat on the basis of atrial activity: in DDI the device paces and senses both chambers but only inhibits; it never tracks the atrium: A.
In the picture, the lower drummer turns his back on the upper one and beats only when the engine room falls silent.
Mode switching does the same during atrial tachyarrhythmias, so the ventricle does not follow a racing atrium, the trembling Pinocchio.
Pacemaker-dependent patients are programmed to an asynchronous mode before surgery, because electrocautery can inhibit pacing.
Electromagnetic interference, also from TENS units, can stop pacing or shocks, damage the lead-tissue interface, reset the device or trigger inappropriate ICD shocks.
Memory hook: in DDI the lower drummer never copies the upper one.
